summary: Geo canary header normalization resets tenant pin leading to mixed-variant routing and degraded fallback
description: Issue summary: During a geo-staggered canary of a new rw-v1.1 variant, tenant session pins were intermittently reset at the edge, causing requests to be routed to the fallback/degraded variant and producing mixed-model outputs for affected users. Impact: Customer Nimbus AI (dedicated) observed inconsistent responses for a subset of traffic (approx 3% of requests), user-visible output drift, and a short-term cost increase due to repeated fallback invocations. Environment: prod (us-west primary, eu-west passive) Canary config: 10% traffic slice, staged over two waves. Observed start: 2026-03-12 03:40 UTC. Current status: In Progress — mitigation applied (edge header preservation, targeted canary pause).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Using a dedicated tenant on prod-us-west, send streaming chat request with X-Tenant-Id and X-Pinned-Model: rw-v1.1 and standard auth headers. 2) Trigger a canary rollout with geo mirror active (us-west->eu-west). 3) Observe routing layer logs at ingress and edge-proxy for model selection and pin state. Expected: persistent pin to rw-v1.1 for the tenant cohort. Actual: intermittent pin reset and routing to rw-open-7b (degraded variant).

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: header normalization during canary mirror (authz sidecar change) is stripping or rewriting X-Pinned-Model for cross-region mirrored requests causing the orchestrator to treat cohort as unpinned. Evidence: matched time windows of canary activation and a deploy on the authz sidecar in us-west (see GH PR/commit below). Correlation: pin resets line up with authz header rewrite logs. Additional evidence: reproducer run with edge debug shows consistent pin retention when authz hook is disabled. Observed anomaly: not all requests were affected — appears to impact mirrored traffic where an auth header refresh triggered a normalization path. Trace ids: trace-ux-77fa, trace-ux-77fb (examples).
comments: 2026-03-12 05:10 - Sophie Tran (Support): Customer reported ~3% of chat sessions returning older-model outputs during canary. Attached session ids and sample payloads.

2026-03-12 06:02 - Miguel Alvarez (SRE): Initial triage — saw header normalization events from authz-sidecar at 03:41 UTC. Reproduced locally by enabling geo-mirror proxy + authz refresh. Hypothesis: header sanitizer is too aggressive for mirrored path.

2026-03-12 09:30 - Eng oncall (Priya Rao): Rollback of authz-sidecar preflight hook to previous behavior in us-west paused further incidents. Requested more telemetry on header mutations and orchestration pin miss reasons.
2026-03-12 11:05 - Customer (Nimbus AI): Confirmed that following the rollback they saw a drop in mixed outputs. Asked for permanent fix and explanation for billing impact from repeated fallbacks.
2026-03-13 02:20 - Miguel Alvarez (SRE): Deployed a targeted edge config to preserve X-Pinned-Model for mirrored requests as an interim mitigation. Added metric edge.pinned_header_preserved_count.
2026-03-14 08:45 - Sophie Tran (Support): Customer accepted the workaround but requested a timeline for a fix and postmortem.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation: rolled back aggressive authz header normalization in us-west and applied edge config to preserve X-Pinned-Model for mirror paths. Root cause: a change in the authz sidecar preflight logic introduced a header sanitize rule that removed X-Pinned-Model on mirrored requests when Authorization token refresh was performed, causing the orchestrator to treat requests as unpinned and select fallback variants. Permanent fix planned: 1) update authz-sidecar to exclude X-Pinned-Model from normalization rules and add a unit/integration test for mirrored paths (PR in progress). 2) add orchestration safeguard to prefer explicit pin header present in original request over mirror-modified headers (config flag and test). 3) increase pin-cohort TTL briefly during canary windows to reduce sensitivity to transient header mutations. 4) update runbook and add metric alarm on pin_miss_rate > 0.5%.
postmortem_followups:
- Merge PR to authz-sidecar to whitelist pinned headers (GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/authz-sidecar/pull/317).
- Add orchestration unit tests for mirrored header precedence.
- Update canary playbook to include header-preservation verification before wave 2.
- Notify Nimbus AI of credit for cost delta during incident and provide detailed billing breakdown.
- Create dashboards: edge.pinned_header_preserved_count, orchestrator.pin_miss_rate, canary.pin_stability_by_cohort.
